question: Where can I get the routes (geometry) of natural gas transmission and distribution pipelines in the United States, with operator, diameter or pressure, and status?

answer.summary: No public US dataset gives full transmission and distribution routes with diameter, pressure, and status. For open national transmission geometry, operator, and operating status, use EIA's ArcGIS FeatureServer (32,892 lines, no diameter/pressure/distribution). PHMSA's statutory NPMS collects authoritative transmission geometry, DIAMETER, and AF/AU/PA status, but restricts GIS exports and DIAMETER to government/operators (public viewer is scale-capped at 1:24,000 and excludes distribution and MAOP). Select states add transmission detail (Texas RRC exposes diameter and status); GEM GGIT and OSM partially fill transmission diameter; distribution mains and MAOP remain non-public.
main_caveats: NPMS excludes gas distribution and gathering entirely (49 CFR 191.29), restricts GIS downloads to govt/operators, caps Public Viewer at 1:24,000 with +/-500 ft accuracy, and withholds DIAMETER from the public.

Open national EIA FeatureServer (32,892 features) derives from FERC Form 567 and public sources (~2020 snapshot reviewed by Esri in 2025): no diameter, no pressure, only Status='Operating', and 0 Gathering despite text claims.
Pressure (MAOP) is absent from NPMS, EIA, and TX RRC; FERC Form 567 (18 CFR 260.8) MAOP flow diagrams are withheld as non-public Critical Energy Infrastructure Information (CEII).

Exact local distribution geometry is withheld for security nationwide (only CO PUC PSPMS exposes one state in a scale-capped viewer); use 811 One-Call for excavation locates or dockets for individual projects.
answer.confidence_reason: Verified across 49 CFR 191 / 18 CFR 260.8 on eCFR, NPMS standards/data dictionary, live API queries on EIA and 7 states, 2 Geofabrik OSM extracts, GEM XLSX/headers, Rextag landing page, and 32 searches.

steps: 1. If you are a federal/state/local/tribal government official or pipeline operator, apply for MFA PIMMA access or a GIS Data Request for your jurisdiction/assets (CUI handling applies).

2. Otherwise, use the NPMS Public Map Viewer county-by-county (cannot zoom closer than ~1:24,000; DIAMETER not shown) and pair with NPMS_Active_Pipe_County_Mileage.xlsx for verified county/operator mileages.
reading_traps: Spatial accuracy is +/-500 feet (upgrading to +/-50-100 ft in Phase 3 by 2027) — explicitly unusable for locating lines before digging (must call 811).
NPMS Active Mileage XLSX explicitly excludes Permanently Abandoned (PA) pipelines, whereas NPMS GIS files include STATUS_CD in {AF, AU, PA}.
Pressure/MAOP is never collected in NPMS (SMYS_S steel yield strength will not be collected before 2028 and is flagged Public: NO).

problems: Public Map Viewer uses reCAPTCHA Enterprise and caps zoom at 1:24,000 (+/-500 ft spatial accuracy until Phase 3 in 2027).
GIS shapefile/GDB exports and DIAMETER (Public: NO) are restricted to approved government officials and pipeline operators via PIMMA.
Excludes gas distribution and gathering; never collects pressure/MAOP; Active Mileage XLSX excludes Permanently Abandoned (PA) lines.

how_to_use.example_request: ogrinfo -q -al /tmp/georutter/us-gas-pipelines/wyoming-latest.osm.pbf -sql "SELECT osm_id, name, other_tags FROM lines WHERE man_made='pipeline'"

steps: 1. Download state .osm.pbf files from Geofabrik US (rhode-island 51 MB, wyoming 92 MB; note larger states exceed 100 MB).
2. Filter GDAL lines layer for man_made='pipeline' AND (other_tags LIKE '%"substance"=>"gas"%' OR '%"substance"=>"natural_gas"%').
3. Exclude unreviewed US Census TIGER stubs (tiger:cfcc without operator or substance) and inspect diameter/location/usage tags.
reading_traps: Legacy TIGER/Line imports (tiger:cfcc='C10', tiger:reviewed='no') create most man_made=pipeline ways in US extracts (RI: 10/81, WY: 23/613) with missing substance and misclassified utility corridors.
Distribution lines are essentially unmapped (0/13 in RI, 0/25 in WY) and pressure tags were 0 in both samples.

problems: Very incomplete coverage across the US; 0 usage=distribution and 0 pressure tags in both sampled states (RI 13 gas ways, WY 25 gas ways).
Polluted by unreviewed 2007-2008 Census TIGER/Line utility corridor ways (tiger:cfcc without substance/operator).
Public Overpass mirrors and Ohsome bbox queries timed out or returned 403/406/504; state PBF extracts needed (larger states >100 MB).

evidence.claim: Geofabrik state PBF extracts analyzed via ogrinfo (RI 52,544,585 B: 81 pipeline ways, 13 gas, 12 operator, 0 diameter, 0 pressure, 0 distribution; WY 95,733,695 B: 613 pipeline ways, 25 gas, 15 operator, 7 diameter, 0 pressure, 0 distribution).

recipe: 1. Obtain federal/state transmission baseline routes from EIA FeatureServer (32,892 rows) and state GIS layers (e.g., TX RRC Layer 14 for diameter and Abandoned/In Service status).

2. For missing diameter/MAOP/capacity on recent or proposed interstate pipelines, query the Federal Register API (agency=federal-energy-regulatory-commission) for blanket certificates, NGA Section 7 notices, and EIS notices, plus EIA Pipeline Projects XLSX (217 project rows with diameter and status).
3. Extract Docket Nos. (e.g. CP26-565-000), operator, county/state, pipe diameter (inches), length (miles), and status from the Federal Register HTML/PDF and matching EPA EIS filings.

4. For qualified government/operator researchers needing official transmission diameters nationwide, apply for NPMS PIMMA/GIS access; for specific intrastate distribution corridors or excavation checks, file state PUC public-record/NDA requests or submit 811 One-Call tickets.

local_terms.meaning: Mandatory PHMSA federal GIS database for gas transmission and LNG under 49 CFR 191.29; excludes distribution and gathering.
NPMS Pipeline Information Management and Mapping Application; restricted MFA web GIS for government officials and pipeline operators.
Unique 5-digit PHMSA Operator Identification number used across NPMS and annual reports.
Maximum operating pressure limit; collected on FERC Form 567 (>100,000 Mcf/d) as non-public CEII, absent from NPMS.
FERC security classification exempting detailed pipeline engineering/flow diagrams (like Form 567) from public FOIA disclosure.
Regulated utility operating local natural gas distribution mains and service lines; 1,335 operators in PHMSA GD AR 2024.
State-mandated pre-excavation utility locate service; the only mechanism to obtain exact local distribution line markings on the ground.
Annual System Flow Diagram filing under 18 CFR 260.8 showing diameter and MAOP for major interstate gas pipelines.
